- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) for 3+ consecutive days, model frequently fails to reflect mean reversion; force forecast to align with 10-day moving average of prior 10 days.
- When model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment: if sentiment is positive, allow slight overshoot; if negative, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30-day moving average of history, adjust forecast to match 30-day MA unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.5) and model is underestimating, add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days; if sentiment is falling, reduce by 1–2%.
- Avoid forecasting >10% above recent 18-day high unless sentiment is >0.7 and volatility is high (e.g., >2% daily range).
